pages.text: Every Monday in the dry season, the pepper seedlings in the JHS nursery drooped in dry soil. But when someone left a tap trickling all weekend, the bed flooded and water was wasted. At Friday’s Computing and Career Technology club, Dzifa had an idea. “We have a 5-volt robotics kit. Let us build a waterer that thinks.” She explained the three parts. “A sensor is the input: it measures how wet the soil is. The microcontroller is the brain: it runs our program. And a small pump is the actuator: it does the physical work.”

At Friday’s Computing and Career Technology club, Dzifa had an idea.
“We have a 5-volt robotics kit.
Let us build a waterer that thinks.” She explained the three parts.
“A sensor is the input: it measures how wet the soil is.
The microcontroller is the brain: it runs our program.
And a small pump is the actuator: it does the physical work.”
pages.alt: Beside a school nursery bed of pepper plants, Dzifa, Sugri, and Kweku inspect a 5-volt robotics kit showing a two-prong soil-moisture sensor, a microcontroller board, and mini tubing.

pages.text: Sir Acheampong would not let them write any code yet. “First, the algorithm,” he said. “Draw it as a flowchart.” Dzifa used the standard symbols: an oval for Start and Stop, a parallelogram for input and output, a rectangle for a process, and a diamond for a yes-or-no decision. Her flowchart read: Start. Read moisturePercent. Decision: is moisturePercent less than 35? If yes, switch the pump on for 10 seconds. If no, keep it off. Wait 10 minutes, then read again. “One more thing,” Dzifa added. “We need a daily limit, and the pump must stop if the tank is empty. Otherwise one fault could flood the bed.”

pages.text: Sugri built the circuit on the battery-powered 5-volt kit, with Sir Acheampong watching. He connected the small pump through a driver circuit, because the microcontroller cannot power a pump directly. Then he added a green light-emitting diode (LED) to show when the pump was running. He put a 220-ohm resistor in series with it, so that too much current would not burn it out. The longer leg of the LED, the positive one, went towards the positive supply. Last, he laid thin tubing along the bed, with a small outlet beside each pepper plant. The water would drip straight to the roots.

pages.text: Would the drum hold enough water for a three-day weekend? The team estimated 12 litres a day, so they needed 36 litres. Kweku measured inside the drum. The radius was 20 cm, and the water stood 70 cm high. A drum is a cylinder, so he used the formula V = πr²h, taking π as 22/7. V = 22/7 × 20 × 20 × 70 = 88,000 cm³. Since 1,000 cm³ make 1 litre, the drum held 88 litres. That was more than twice what they needed.

pages.text: During testing, Sugri took five quick moisture readings: 31, 32, 32, 33, and 97. The 97 was a glitch. A loose wire had touched wet metal for a moment. “Look what it does to the mean,” said Dzifa. “31 + 32 + 32 + 33 + 97 = 225, and 225 ÷ 5 = 45. The controller would think the dry soil was wet and refuse to water it.” The 97 was an outlier, a value far from all the others. “Use the median instead,” she said. “Put the readings in order and take the middle one: 32. One bad reading cannot move it.” They fixed the wire and programmed the controller to use the median of five readings.

pages.text: On Tuesday morning, after a long holiday weekend, the three friends ran to the nursery. The mark on the drum showed about 52 litres left, so close to 36 litres had been used, just as they had estimated. The log showed short bursts of watering whenever the median reading fell below 35%. Every pepper seedling stood firm and dark green. Sir Acheampong beamed. “The algorithm gave it logic. Career Technology built it safely. And Mathematics sized the tank and caught the faulty reading.”

activities.question: In a standard Computing flowchart, which geometric symbol represents a conditional Decision such as "Is moisturePercent < 35?"
options: A diamond shape with branches for Yes (True) and No (False)
A rounded oval used only at Start and Stop
A plain straight arrow without any text

activities.question: Why did Sugri connect a 220-ohm resistor in series with the light-emitting diode (LED) on the 5-volt circuit?
options: To convert plastic PVC pipes into copper wires
To limit electric current flowing through the LED so it does not burn out
To increase the voltage from 5 V up to 230 V mains

activities.question: A cylindrical bucket has internal radius r = 14 cm and height h = 50 cm (take π = 22/7, 1,000 cm³ = 1 L). What is its volume in litres?

activities.prompt: Put the steps of the smart watering cycle in the correct order.
items: Sensor probes detect five moisture readings from the root zone.
Microcontroller sorts readings and picks median, ignoring outliers.
Conditional rule evaluates whether median moisture is below 35%.
When True, controller switches on indicator LED and mini DC pump.
